question: What is the primary purpose of an Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

options.A: To store health insurance billing information for government agencies
options.B: To replace traditional bedside nursing care with automated tasks
options.C: To store a patient's digital medical history for authorized sharing
options.D: To provide patients with a private diary of their daily symptoms

explanation: An EHR is a digital chart designed primarily to collect and safely share comprehensive patient health information among healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h1)

question: How do Electronic Health Records mainly improve teamwork among healthcare professionals?

options.A: By eliminating the need for nurses and doctors to ever speak to each other
options.B: By replacing all physical bedside shift handovers with text messages
options.C: By allowing instant access to updated patient notes across different departments
options.D: By automatically deciding the medical diagnosis for every admitted patient

explanation: Instant digital access means doctors, nurses, and pharmacists can see the same up-to-date information simultaneously, improving coordination of care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which system is best described as a digital version of a paper chart limited to a single clinic?
explanation: An EMR is traditionally confined to one practice or facility, functioning mostly like a digital paper chart for that specific location. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the main advantage of an EHR over an EMR?

options.A: An EHR is cheaper to install and requires no electricity or computer network
options.B: An EHR is designed to share patient data across multiple different healthcare organizations
options.C: An EHR requires physical paper backup files for every single digital entry
options.D: An EHR can only be accessed by medical doctors and never by nursing staff

explanation: The key benefit of an EHR is interoperability, meaning information flows seamlessly across different hospitals, clinics, and specialists. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h2)

question: What does CPOE stand for in health informatics?
explanation: CPOE is the electronic system clinicians use to input medical orders directly, replacing messy handwritten prescriptions. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h3)

question: How does a Clinical Decision Support (CDS) feature protect hospitalized patients?

options.A: By printing out paper charts for family members to review at home
options.B: By automatically ordering emergency laboratory tests without doctor approval
options.C: By locking the computer screen whenever a nurse leaves the patient bedside
options.D: By popping up automated warnings about drug allergies or unsafe medication dosages

explanation: CDS tools act as safety nets by analyzing patient data in real time and alerting staff to potential clinical risks before harm occurs. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h3)

question: A nurse uses a bedside scanner to check a patient's wristband and a medication package before giving a pill. What safety feature is being used?
explanation: Scanning patient wristbands and medication packages prevents administration errors by verifying the right patient, drug, and dose. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why is the elimination of handwritten nursing notes considered a major safety improvement?

options.A: It makes paper storage rooms completely unnecessary in every hospital
options.B: It allows computers to automatically write the discharge summary for the doctor
options.C: It prevents medication errors caused by misreading unclear handwriting
options.D: It ensures that nurses never make any clinical documentation mistakes

explanation: Clear digital text removes the guesswork and dangerous mistakes that frequently arise from reading messy or faded handwriting on paper charts. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is a major infrastructure challenge facing EHR implementation in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Unstable power supply and unreliable internet connectivity
options.B: Complete refusal of patients to allow digital data collection
options.C: Too many software options created by local nursing students
options.D: An overabundance of computer hardware in rural clinics

explanation: Consistent electricity and internet access are essential for digital health records, making power outages a major operational barrier. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why do some experienced healthcare staff initially resist shifting from paper charts to electronic health records?

options.A: They are legally forbidden by hospital policy from touching computer keyboards
options.B: They believe digital records make patient care completely invisible to doctors
options.C: They are comfortable with traditional paper habits and fear learning complex new software
options.D: They prefer spending extra hours manually searching through heavy filing cabinets

explanation: Change management is difficult because staff accustomed to paper workflows often feel intimidated or inconvenienced by new technology. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the function of an audit trail in an electronic health record system?

options.A: To measure how fast patients recover from surgical procedures
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of hospital supplies used daily
options.C: To track and record every user who opens, views, or edits a patient file
options.D: To automatically generate monthly nursing staff duty rosters and shifts

explanation: Audit trails record digital footprints, showing precisely who accessed a patient's record and when, which deters unauthorized snooping. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard security measure used to protect electronic patient records?

options.A: Publicly posting patient medical histories on hospital hallway notice boards
options.B: Password protection and secure login credentials for every clinician
options.C: Biometric fingerprint scanners to verify staff identity at the workstation
options.D: Role-based access controls that limit file viewing to authorized staff

explanation: Posting private health information publicly violates core confidentiality principles and patient privacy laws. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h6)
